items.q: The most common presentation of hypercalcemia is:
The second most common (chronic) symptom of hypercalcemia is:
Match the mnemonic — 1) Painful 2) Renal 3) Abdominal 4) Psychotic 5) Fatigue … A) Groan B) Bone C) Moans D) Stone E) Overtone
items.exp: Painful-Bone, Renal-Stone, Abdominal-Groan, Psychotic-Moans, Fatigue-Overtone. (Book p878)

items.q: The acute abdominal features (pain, vomiting, constipation) of hypercalcemia mimic:
items.exp: Acute abdominal triad mimics pancreatitis. (Book p878)

items.q: Neuropsychiatric features of acute hypercalcemia include:
ECG — 1) Hypercalcemia  2) Hypocalcemia … A) Long QT interval  B) Short QT interval
items.exp: Hypercalcemia: short QT; hypocalcemia: long QT. (Book p878)

items.q: ‘Diarrhea and seizures are expected findings in hypercalcemia.’
items.exp: In hypercalcemia diarrhea and seizures are NOT seen. (Book p878)

items.q: Chronic renal manifestations of hypercalcemia include:
opts: Nephritic sediment with red cell casts
items.exp: Renal: recurrent stone, recurrent UTI. (Book p878)

items.q: Chronic features include painful bones, myopathy, band keratopathy and pseudoclubbing. Pick the ODD ONE OUT:
items.exp: Drowsiness is acute; band keratopathy, pseudoclubbing, myopathy are chronic. (Book p878)

items.q: Neurogenic diabetes insipidus in hypercalcemia leads sequentially to:
items.exp: Neurogenic DI → polyuria → dehydration → pre-renal AKI. (Book p878)

items.q: The other renal presentation of hypercalcemia, besides neurogenic DI, is:
items.exp: Renal presentation: neurogenic DI and chronic tubulointerstitial disease. (Book p878)
